title: What Graph Unlearning Cannot Erase: Physics-Induced Leakage of Cyberattack Information in Electric Vehicle Charging Networks
abstract: arXiv:2606.19566v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) can expose distribution feeders to cyberattacks. While machine learning methods, including graph neural networks (GNNs), can localize which bus is compromised, significant challenges remain in data sharing and model training. For example, data-sharing agreements grant EVCS operators the right to withdraw their charging power for privacy or security reasons from a deployed model, yet retraining from scratch on every request would repeat the full-retraining (FR) cost. To address this, we study graph unlearning (GU) for EVCS cyberattack localization, formulated as a feature-level unlearning problem on a graph-level multi-label classification task. We benchmark fine-tuning (FT) against two GU baselines on the IEEE 34-bus, 123-bus, and 8500-node distribution networks across three GNN backbones and cumulative unlearning scenarios. translated_title: 图遗忘无法抹去的内容：电动汽车充电网络中由物理规律导致的网络攻击信息泄露
translated_abstract: 电动汽车充电站（EVCS）可能使配电馈线面临网络攻击风险。尽管包括图神经网络（GNN）在内的机器学习方法能够定位哪个母线遭到入侵，但在数据共享和模型训练方面仍存在重大挑战。例如，数据共享协议赋予EVCS运营商基于隐私或安全原因从已部署模型中撤回其充电功率的权利，但若每次请求都从头重新训练，将重复完全重新训练（FR）的成本。为解决这一问题，我们研究用于EVCS网络攻击定位的图遗忘（GU），将其表述为图级多标签分类任务上的特征级遗忘问题。我们在IEEE 34节点、123节点和8500节点配电网络上，针对三种GNN骨干网络和累积遗忘场景，将微调（FT）与两种GU基线方法进行基准对比。实验表明，经过遗忘处理或在不包含被撤回数据的情况下重新训练的GNN……（原文摘要到此截断）
tldr: 该论文将图遗忘技术应用于电动汽车充电站的网络攻击定位任务，并揭示了即便执行了遗忘操作，网络攻击信息仍会经由电网的物理规律发生泄露，无法被完全抹除。
en_tdlr: This paper applies graph unlearning to cyberattack localization in EV charging networks and reveals that cyberattack information cannot be fully erased, as it leaks through physics-induced dependencies in the power grid.
